sanskrit: pāṇḍavāpi tato rājañ śrutvā taṃ ninadaṃ mahat dadhmuḥ śaṅkhāṃś ca bherīś ca murajāṃś ca vyanādayan
english: And the Pāṇḍavas too, O king, on hearing that mighty din, blew their conches and sounded their kettledrums and tabours.

sanskrit: dhṛtarāṣṭra uvāca pratijñāte tu bhīṣmeṇa tasmin yuddhe sudāruṇe krodhito mama putreṇa duḥkhitena viśeṣataḥ
english: Dhṛtarāṣṭra said: When Bhīṣma had taken his vow in that most terrible battle, having been provoked to wrath—especially by my grieving son—

sanskrit: bhīṣmaḥ kim akarot tatra pāṇḍaveyeṣu saṃjaya pitāmahe vā pāñcālās tan mamācakṣva saṃjaya
english: what then did Bhīṣma do among the Pāṇḍavas, O Saṃjaya, and what did the Pāñcālas do against the grandsire? Tell me that, Saṃjaya.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca gatapūrvāhṇabhūyiṣṭhe tasminn ahani bhārata jayaṃ prāpteṣu hṛṣṭeṣu pāṇḍaveṣu mahātmasu
english: Saṃjaya said: When the greater part of the forenoon of that day had passed, O Bhārata, and the great-souled Pāṇḍavas, having gained the advantage, were exultant,

sanskrit: sarvadharmaviśeṣajñaḥ pitā devavratas tava abhyayāj javanair aśvaiḥ pāṇḍavānām anīkinīm mahatyā senayā guptas tava putraiś ca sarvaśaḥ
english: your father Devavrata, knower of all the finer points of duty, advanced with swift horses against the host of the Pāṇḍavas, guarded by a great army and by your sons on every side.

sanskrit: prāvartata tato yuddhaṃ tumulaṃ lomaharṣaṇam asmākaṃ pāṇḍavaiḥ sārdham anayāt tava bhārata
english: Then there began a tumultuous, hair-raising battle between us and the Pāṇḍavas, born of your folly, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: dhanuṣāṃ kūjatāṃ tatra talānāṃ cābhihanyatām mahān samabhavac chabdo girīṇām iva dīryatām
english: From the twanging of bows and the clapping of bowstring-guards there arose a mighty sound there, as of mountains splitting apart.

sanskrit: tiṣṭha sthito 'smi viddhy enaṃ nivartasva sthiro bhava sthito 'smi praharasveti śabdāḥ śrūyanta sarvaśaḥ
english: "Stand! I am standing! Strike this man! Turn back! Hold firm! I am at my post! Smite away!"—such cries were heard on every side.

sanskrit: kāñcaneṣu tanutreṣu kirīṭeṣu dhvajeṣu ca śilānām iva śaileṣu patitānām abhūt svanaḥ
english: Upon the golden coats of mail, the diadems, and the banners there arose a clatter, like that of rocks falling upon mountains.

sanskrit: patitāny uttamāṅgāni bāhavaś ca vibhūṣitāḥ vyaceṣṭanta mahīṃ prāpya śataśo 'tha sahasraśaḥ
english: Heads cut off and ornamented arms, fallen by the hundreds and by the thousands, writhed upon the ground when they reached it.

sanskrit: hṛtottamāṅgāḥ ke cit tu tathaivodyatakārmukāḥ pragṛhītāyudhāś cāpi tasthuḥ puruṣasattamāḥ
english: Some of those foremost of men, though their heads had been struck off, stood yet with bows raised and weapons grasped firm.

sanskrit: prāvartata mahāvegā nadī rudhiravāhinī mātaṅgāṅgaśilāraudrā māṃsaśoṇitakardamā
english: A river of swift current began to flow, bearing blood, dreadful with the limbs of elephants for its rocks, its mire of flesh and gore.

sanskrit: varāśvanaranāgānāṃ śarīraprabhavā tadā paralokārṇavamukhī gṛdhragomāyumodinī
english: Springing then from the bodies of fine horses, men, and elephants, it flowed toward the ocean of the other world, gladdening vultures and jackals.

sanskrit: na dṛṣṭaṃ na śrutaṃ cāpi yuddham etādṛśaṃ nṛpa yathā tava sutānāṃ ca pāṇḍavānāṃ ca bhārata
english: Never was such a battle seen or heard of, O king, as that of your sons and of the Pāṇḍavas, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: nāsīd rathapathas tatra yodhair yudhi nipātitaiḥ gajaiś ca patitair nīlair giriśṛṅgair ivāvṛtam
english: No path remained there for chariots, so covered was it with warriors struck down in the fight and with fallen dark elephants, like mountain peaks.

sanskrit: vikīrṇaiḥ kavacaiś citrair dhvajaiś chatraiś ca māriṣa śuśubhe tad raṇasthānaṃ śaradīva nabhastalam
english: With scattered, gleaming mail, with banners and parasols, O sire, that field of battle shone like the vault of heaven in autumn.

sanskrit: vinirbhinnāḥ śaraiḥ ke cid antapīḍāvikarṣiṇaḥ abhītāḥ samare śatrūn abhyadhāvanta daṃśitāḥ
english: Some, pierced through by arrows and dragging their wounds in their last agony, yet fearless and mailed, rushed upon the foe in battle.

sanskrit: tāta bhrātaḥ sakhe bandho vayasya mama mātula mā māṃ parityajety anye cukruśuḥ patitā raṇe
english: "Father! Brother! Friend! Kinsman! Comrade! My uncle! Do not abandon me!"—so cried others who had fallen in the fight.

sanskrit: ādhāvābhyehi mā gaccha kiṃ bhīto 'si kva yāsyasi sthito 'haṃ samare mā bhair iti cānye vicukruśuḥ
english: "Charge! Come on! Do not flee! Why are you afraid? Where are you going? I stand here in the battle—fear not!"—thus others cried aloud.

sanskrit: tatra bhīṣmaḥ śāṃtanavo nityaṃ maṇḍalakārmukaḥ mumoca bāṇān dīptāgrān ahīn āśīviṣān iva
english: There Bhīṣma, son of Śaṃtanu, his bow ever bent into a circle, loosed arrows blazing at the tips, like venomous serpents.

sanskrit: śarair ekāyanīkurvan diśaḥ sarvā yatavrataḥ jaghāna pāṇḍavarathān ādiśyādiśya bhārata
english: Making all the quarters one solid mass of arrows, that firm-vowed one slew the chariot-warriors of the Pāṇḍavas, marking out one after another, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: sa nṛtyan vai rathopasthe darśayan pāṇilāghavam alātacakravad rājaṃs tatra tatra sma dṛśyate
english: Dancing, as it were, upon his chariot-platform and displaying the swiftness of his hands, he appeared here and there, O king, like a whirling firebrand.

sanskrit: tam ekaṃ samare śūraṃ pāṇḍavāḥ sṛñjayās tathā anekaśatasāhasraṃ samapaśyanta lāghavāt
english: That single hero in battle the Pāṇḍavas and the Sṛñjayas beheld, by reason of his swiftness, as if he were many hundreds of thousands.

sanskrit: māyākṛtātmānam iva bhīṣmaṃ tatra sma menire pūrvasyāṃ diśi taṃ dṛṣṭvā pratīcyāṃ dadṛśur janāḥ
english: They reckoned Bhīṣma there to have multiplied himself by magic; for having seen him in the east, men beheld him in the west.

sanskrit: udīcyāṃ cainam ālokya dakṣiṇasyāṃ punaḥ prabho evaṃ sa samare vīro gāṅgeyaḥ pratyadṛśyata
english: Beholding him in the north, they saw him again in the south, O lord; thus did that hero, the son of Gaṅgā, show himself in the battle.

sanskrit: na cainaṃ pāṇḍaveyānāṃ kaś cic chaknoti vīkṣitum viśikhān eva paśyanti bhīṣmacāpacyutān bahūn
english: None among the Pāṇḍavas was able even to look upon him; they saw only the many shafts loosed from Bhīṣma's bow.

sanskrit: kurvāṇaṃ samare karma sūdayānaṃ ca vāhinīm vyākrośanta raṇe tatra vīrā bahuvidhaṃ bahu amānuṣeṇa rūpeṇa carantaṃ pitaraṃ tava
english: Beholding him working his feats in battle and destroying their host—your father ranging there in superhuman form—the heroes in that fight wailed aloud in many ways and grievously.

sanskrit: śalabhā iva rājānaḥ patanti vidhicoditāḥ bhīṣmāgnim abhi saṃkruddhaṃ vināśāya sahasraśaḥ
english: Like locusts, the kings fell, driven on by fate, by the thousands into the wrathful fire that was Bhīṣma, to their own destruction.

sanskrit: na hi moghaḥ śaraḥ kaś cid āsīd bhīṣmasya saṃyuge naranāgāśvakāyeṣu bahutvāl laghuvedhinaḥ
english: For no shaft of Bhīṣma's was ever in vain in that combat; piercing keenly, by reason of the multitude of bodies of men, elephants, and horses, none missed its mark.

sanskrit: bhinatty ekena bāṇena sumuktena patatriṇā gajakaṅkaṭasaṃnāhaṃ vajreṇevācalottamam
english: With a single well-loosed feathered arrow he would pierce an elephant's mail and armour, as a thunderbolt cleaves the loftiest mountain.

sanskrit: dvau trīn api gajārohān piṇḍitān varmitān api nārācena sutīkṣṇena nijaghāna pitā tava
english: Two and even three elephant-riders, packed close together and armoured though they were, your father slew with a single keen iron shaft.

sanskrit: yo yo bhīṣmaṃ naravyāghram abhyeti yudhi kaś cana muhūrtadṛṣṭaḥ sa mayā pātito bhuvi dṛśyate
english: Whoever came against Bhīṣma, that tiger among men, in the fight, was seen by me but for a moment, and then beheld struck down upon the earth.

sanskrit: evaṃ sā dharmarājasya vadhyamānā mahācamūḥ bhīṣmeṇātulavīryeṇa vyaśīryata sahasradhā
english: Thus that great army of the Dharma-king, slaughtered by Bhīṣma of matchless valour, was shattered into a thousand pieces.

sanskrit: prakīryata mahāsenā śaravarṣābhitāpitā paśyato vāsudevasya pārthasya ca mahātmanaḥ
english: That mighty host, scorched by the rain of arrows, was scattered before the very eyes of Vāsudeva and of the great-souled Pārtha.

sanskrit: yatamānāpi te vīrā dravamāṇān mahārathān nāśaknuvan vārayituṃ bhīṣmabāṇaprapīḍitāḥ
english: Though they strove, those heroes, tormented by Bhīṣma's arrows, could not check the great chariot-warriors who were fleeing.

sanskrit: mahendrasamavīryeṇa vadhyamānā mahācamūḥ abhajyata mahārāja na ca dvau saha dhāvataḥ
english: Slaughtered by him whose valour equalled great Indra's, the mighty host broke, O great king, and not even two fled together.

sanskrit: āviddhanaranāgāśvaṃ patitadhvajakūbaram anīkaṃ pāṇḍuputrāṇāṃ hāhābhūtam acetanam
english: With its men, elephants, and horses pierced through, its banners and chariot-poles fallen, the army of Pāṇḍu's sons grew senseless and broke into cries of woe.

sanskrit: jaghānātra pitā putraṃ putraś ca pitaraṃ tathā priyaṃ sakhāyaṃ cākrande sakhā daivabalātkṛtaḥ
english: There, compelled by the force of fate, father slew son and son slew father, and friend struck down his dear friend amid the wailing.

sanskrit: vimucya kavacān anye pāṇḍuputrasya sainikāḥ prakīrya keśān dhāvantaḥ pratyadṛśyanta bhārata
english: Others among the soldiers of Pāṇḍu's son were seen casting off their armour and fleeing with hair dishevelled, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: tad gokulam ivodbhrāntam udbhrāntarathayūthapam dadṛśe pāṇḍuputrasya sainyam ārtasvaraṃ tadā
english: Like a herd of cattle in panic, its chariot-leaders thrown into confusion, the army of Pāṇḍu's son was then seen, raised in cries of anguish.

sanskrit: prabhajyamānaṃ tat sainyaṃ dṛṣṭvā devakinandanaḥ uvāca pārthaṃ bībhatsuṃ nigṛhya ratham uttamam
english: Seeing that army breaking apart, the son of Devakī, reining in the splendid chariot, spoke to Pārtha, the Bībhatsu:

sanskrit: ayaṃ sa kālaḥ saṃprāptaḥ pārtha yaḥ kāṅkṣitas tvayā praharāsmai naravyāghra na cen mohād vimuhyase
english: "The hour has come, O Pārtha, that you have longed for. Strike at him, O tiger among men, unless you are bewildered by delusion!

sanskrit: yat tvayā kathitaṃ vīra purā rājñāṃ samāgame bhīṣmadroṇamukhān sarvān dhārtarāṣṭrasya sainikān
english: What you declared of old, O hero, in the assembly of kings—that you would slay all the warriors of Dhṛtarāṣṭra's son, headed by Bhīṣma and Droṇa,

sanskrit: sānubandhān haniṣyāmi ye māṃ yotsyanti saṃyuge iti tat kuru kaunteya satyaṃ vākyam ariṃdama
english: with their followers—all who would do battle with me—that make true now, O son of Kuntī, that word of yours, O scorcher of foes!"

sanskrit: bībhatso paśya sainyaṃ svaṃ bhajyamānaṃ samantataḥ dravataś ca mahīpālān sarvān yaudhiṣṭhire bale
english: "O Bībhatsu, behold your own army breaking on every side, and all the lords of earth in Yudhiṣṭhira's host taking to flight.

sanskrit: dṛṣṭvā hi samare bhīṣmaṃ vyāttānanam ivāntakam bhayārtāḥ saṃpraṇaśyanti siṃhaṃ kṣudramṛgā iva
english: For seeing Bhīṣma in battle, like Death with jaws agape, they perish in their terror, as little beasts before a lion."

sanskrit: evam uktaḥ pratyuvāca vāsudevaṃ dhanaṃjayaḥ codayāśvān yato bhīṣmo vigāhyaitad balārṇavam
english: Thus addressed, Dhanaṃjaya answered Vāsudeva: "Plunging into this ocean of troops, drive the horses to where Bhīṣma is."

sanskrit: tato 'śvān rajataprakhyāṃś codayām āsa mādhavaḥ yato bhīṣmaratho rājan duṣprekṣyo raśmimān iva
english: Then Mādhava urged on the silver-hued steeds toward where Bhīṣma's chariot stood, O king, hard to gaze upon as the radiant sun.

sanskrit: tatas tat punar āvṛttaṃ yudhiṣṭhirabalaṃ mahat dṛṣṭvā pārthaṃ mahābāhuṃ bhīṣmāyodyantam āhave
english: Then that great host of Yudhiṣṭhira rallied once more, seeing the mighty-armed Pārtha rising up against Bhīṣma in the battle.

sanskrit: tato bhīṣmaḥ kuruśreṣṭhaḥ siṃhavad vinadan muhuḥ dhanaṃjayarathaṃ tūrṇaṃ śaravarṣair avākirat
english: Then Bhīṣma, foremost of the Kurus, roaring again and again like a lion, swiftly covered the chariot of Dhanaṃjaya with showers of arrows.

sanskrit: kṣaṇena sa rathas tasya sahayaḥ sahasārathiḥ śaravarṣeṇa mahatā saṃchanno na prakāśate
english: In a moment that chariot of his, with its horses and its driver, veiled by the great rain of shafts, was no longer to be seen.

sanskrit: vāsudevas tv asaṃbhrānto dhairyam āsthāya sattvavān codayām āsa tān aśvān vitunnān bhīṣmasāyakaiḥ
english: But Vāsudeva, unflinching, holding firm with steadfast resolve, urged on those horses, sorely wounded by Bhīṣma's arrows.

sanskrit: tataḥ pārtho dhanur gṛhya divyaṃ jaladanisvanam pātayām āsa bhīṣmasya dhanuś chittvā tribhiḥ śaraiḥ
english: Then Pārtha, taking up his celestial bow that roared like a thundercloud, cut Bhīṣma's bow with three arrows and brought it down.

sanskrit: sa cchinnadhanvā kauravyaḥ punar anyan mahad dhanuḥ nimeṣāntaramātreṇa sajyaṃ cakre pitā tava
english: His bow thus severed, the Kaurava—your father—in the mere span between two blinks strung yet another great bow.

sanskrit: vicakarṣa tato dorbhyāṃ dhanur jaladanisvanam athāsya tad api kruddhaś ciccheda dhanur arjunaḥ
english: Then with both arms he drew that bow that thundered like a cloud; but Arjuna, wrathful, cut that bow of his too.

sanskrit: tasya tat pūjayām āsa lāghavaṃ śaṃtanoḥ sutaḥ sādhu pārtha mahābāho sādhu bho pāṇḍunandana
english: The son of Śaṃtanu applauded that swiftness of his: "Well done, mighty-armed Pārtha! Well done, O delight of Pāṇḍu!

sanskrit: tvayy evaitad yuktarūpaṃ mahat karma dhanaṃjaya prīto 'smi sudṛḍhaṃ putra kuru yuddhaṃ mayā saha
english: In you alone, Dhanaṃjaya, does this great feat befit. I am exceedingly pleased, my son—do battle with me!"

sanskrit: iti pārthaṃ praśasyātha pragṛhyānyan mahad dhanuḥ mumoca samare vīraḥ śarān pārtharathaṃ prati
english: Thus praising Pārtha, the hero took up another great bow and loosed his shafts in battle against Pārtha's chariot.

sanskrit: adarśayad vāsudevo hayayāne paraṃ balam moghān kurvañ śarāṃs tasya maṇḍalāny acaral laghu
english: Vāsudeva displayed the highest skill in the driving of the steeds; rendering his shafts vain, he wheeled deftly in circling courses.

sanskrit: tathāpi bhīṣmaḥ sudṛḍhaṃ vāsudevadhanaṃjayau vivyādha niśitair bāṇaiḥ sarvagātreṣu māriṣa
english: Even so, Bhīṣma pierced both Vāsudeva and Dhanaṃjaya hard with whetted arrows in every limb, O sire.

sanskrit: śuśubhāte naravyāghrau tau bhīṣmaśaravikṣatau govṛṣāv iva nardantau viṣāṇollikhitāṅkitau
english: Those two tigers among men, gashed by Bhīṣma's shafts, shone like two bellowing bulls scored and marked by each other's horns.

sanskrit: punaś cāpi susaṃkruddhaḥ śaraiḥ saṃnataparvabhiḥ kṛṣṇayor yudhi saṃrabdho bhīṣmo vyāvārayad diśaḥ
english: And once again, greatly enraged and furious in the fight, Bhīṣma with smooth-jointed arrows shut off all the quarters around the two Kṛṣṇas.

sanskrit: vārṣṇeyaṃ ca śarais tīkṣṇaiḥ kampayām āsa roṣitaḥ muhur abhyutsmayan bhīṣmaḥ prahasya svanavat tadā
english: Wrathful, he made the Vārṣṇeya tremble with keen shafts, while Bhīṣma, smiling again and again, laughed aloud the while.

sanskrit: tataḥ kṛṣṇas tu samare dṛṣṭvā bhīṣmaparākramam saṃprekṣya ca mahābāhuḥ pārthasya mṛduyuddhatām
english: Then Kṛṣṇa, the mighty-armed, beholding in battle the prowess of Bhīṣma, and marking the gentleness of Pārtha's fighting,

sanskrit: bhīṣmaṃ ca śaravarṣāṇi sṛjantam aniśaṃ yudhi pratapantam ivādityaṃ madhyam āsādya senayoḥ
english: and seeing Bhīṣma pouring forth showers of arrows ceaselessly in the fight, blazing like the sun as he reached the midst between the two armies,

sanskrit: varān varān vinighnantaṃ pāṇḍuputrasya sainikān yugāntam iva kurvāṇaṃ bhīṣmaṃ yaudhiṣṭhire bale
english: striking down the best and bravest of the soldiers of Pāṇḍu's son, working as it were the end of an age upon Yudhiṣṭhira's host—

sanskrit: amṛṣyamāṇo bhagavān keśavaḥ paravīrahā acintayad ameyātmā nāsti yaudhiṣṭhiraṃ balam
english: the blessed Keśava, slayer of hostile heroes, no longer able to bear it, that one of measureless soul, thought: "Yudhiṣṭhira's army is as good as no more.

sanskrit: ekāhnā hi raṇe bhīṣmo nāśayed devadānavān kim u pāṇḍusutān yuddhe sabalān sapadānugān
english: For in a single day Bhīṣma could destroy in battle the gods and dānavas—how much more the sons of Pāṇḍu, with their forces and their followers!

sanskrit: dravate ca mahat sainyaṃ pāṇḍavasya mahātmanaḥ ete ca kauravās tūrṇaṃ prabhagnān dṛśya somakān ādravanti raṇe hṛṣṭā harṣayantaḥ pitāmaham
english: The great army of the high-souled Pāṇḍava is fleeing; and these Kauravas, seeing the Somakas swiftly broken, rush forward in the fight exultant, gladdening the grandsire.

sanskrit: so 'haṃ bhīṣmaṃ nihanmy adya pāṇḍavārthāya daṃśitaḥ bhāram etaṃ vineṣyāmi pāṇḍavānāṃ mahātmanām
english: I myself will slay Bhīṣma this day for the Pāṇḍavas' sake, girt in mail; this burden of the great-souled Pāṇḍavas I shall lift away."

sanskrit: arjuno 'pi śarais tīkṣṇair vadhyamāno hi saṃyuge kartavyaṃ nābhijānāti raṇe bhīṣmasya gauravāt
english: Arjuna too, struck by the keen arrows in the combat, knew not what he should do in the fight, out of reverence for Bhīṣma.

sanskrit: tathā cintayatas tasya bhūya eva pitāmahaḥ preṣayām āsa saṃkruddhaḥ śarān pārtharathaṃ prati
english: As he was thinking thus, the grandsire, enraged, once more let fly his arrows against Pārtha's chariot.

sanskrit: teṣāṃ bahutvād dhi bhṛśaṃ śarāṇāṃ; diśo 'tha sarvāḥ pihitā babhūvuḥ na cāntarikṣaṃ na diśo na bhūmir; na bhāskaro 'dṛśyata raśmimālī vavuś ca vātās tumulāḥ sadhūmā; diśaś ca sarvāḥ kṣubhitā babhūvuḥ
english: By the very multitude of those arrows all the quarters were utterly veiled; neither sky nor quarters nor earth could be seen, nor the garland-rayed sun; tumultuous winds laden with smoke arose, and all the quarters were thrown into turmoil.

sanskrit: droṇo vikarṇo 'tha jayadrathaś ca; bhūriśravāḥ kṛtavarmā kṛpaś ca śrutāyur ambaṣṭhapatiś ca rājā; vindānuvindau ca sudakṣiṇaś ca
english: Droṇa and Vikarṇa, and Jayadratha, Bhūriśravas, Kṛtavarman, and Kṛpa, King Śrutāyus and the lord of the Ambaṣṭhas, and Vinda and Anuvinda, and Sudakṣiṇa,

sanskrit: prācyāś ca sauvīragaṇāś ca sarve; vasātayaḥ kṣudrakamālavāś ca kirīṭinaṃ tvaramāṇābhisasrur; nideśagāḥ śāṃtanavasya rājñaḥ
english: and all the men of the East and the hosts of the Sauvīras, the Vasātis, and the Kṣudrakas and Mālavas—obedient to the command of King Śaṃtanu's son—hastened against the Diademed One.

sanskrit: taṃ vājipādātarathaughajālair; anekasāhasraśatair dadarśa kirīṭinaṃ saṃparivāryamāṇaṃ; śiner naptā vāraṇayūthapaiś ca
english: The grandson of Śini beheld the Diademed One being hemmed in by floods and nets of horse, foot, and chariots, by many hundreds of thousands, and by leaders of elephant-herds.

sanskrit: tatas tu dṛṣṭvārjunavāsudevau; padātināgāśvarathaiḥ samantāt abhidrutau śastrabhṛtāṃ variṣṭhau; śinipravīro 'bhisasāra tūrṇam
english: Then, seeing Arjuna and Vāsudeva, those foremost of weapon-bearers, beset on every side by foot, elephants, horse, and chariots, the hero of the Śinis swiftly advanced.

sanskrit: sa tāny anīkāni mahādhanuṣmāñ; śinipravīraḥ sahasābhipatya cakāra sāhāyyam athārjunasya; viṣṇur yathā vṛtraniṣūdanasya
english: That mighty bowman, the hero of the Śinis, rushing suddenly upon those hosts, came to Arjuna's aid, as Viṣṇu once aided the slayer of Vṛtra.

sanskrit: viśīrṇanāgāśvarathadhvajaughaṃ; bhīṣmeṇa vitrāsitasarvayodham yudhiṣṭhirānīkam abhidravantaṃ; provāca saṃdṛśya śinipravīraḥ
english: Beholding the army of Yudhiṣṭhira, its masses of elephants, horses, chariots, and banners shattered, all its warriors terrified by Bhīṣma, fleeing away, the hero of the Śinis spoke:

sanskrit: kva kṣatriyā yāsyatha naiṣa dharmaḥ; satāṃ purastāt kathitaḥ purāṇaiḥ mā svāṃ pratijñāṃ jahata pravīrāḥ; svaṃ vīradharmaṃ paripālayadhvam
english: "Whither do you go, O kṣatriyas? This is no righteous course; it was proclaimed by the ancients before all good men. Do not forsake your vow, O heroes; uphold your own warrior's duty!"
